definitions.explanation: A speech sound produced without obstruction of airflow. Japanese has five vowels: あ (a), い (i), う (u), え (e), お (o).

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}の{母音|ぼいん}は{五|いつ}つある。
{英語|えいご}は{日本語|にほんご}より{母音|ぼいん}の{数|かず}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: English has more vowels than Japanese.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}では{母音|ぼいん}が{連続|れんぞく}すると{発音|はつおん}しにくくなることがある。
examples.english: In Japanese, when vowels occur in succession, they can become difficult to pronounce.

notes:
USAGE:
A linguistics and language-learning term. Useful when discussing pronunciation differences between Japanese and other languages. Japanese vowels are "pure" (monophthongs), unlike English vowels which often glide (diphthongs).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {母音|ぼいん}の{発音|はつおん}: vowel pronunciation
- {長母音|ちょうぼいん}: long vowel
- {短母音|たんぼいん}: short vowel
- {母音|ぼいん}{調和|ちょうわ}: vowel harmony

CONTRASTING TERM:
- {子音|しいん}: consonant
